_note: THE MEET-UP: a new board family, his idea. The job is turning up; the story is who is there and what they want. Talks at a placed person are built, so most letters need nothing new.

THE PLAYER'S PART: the order you say it in. He gives two things and tells you to say them how you like; she hears the ship first or the apology first, and that is the ending. Today only exchanges[0] can close a talk, so ship-first is built and apology-first waits in _choice (letter to Eliza 2026-11-07). Until it can be chosen this Delve has no player's part, so it stays unbuilt.
Voices borrowed until his ear casts them. No names, places or currency in any voiced line.

LETTER d: THE GO-BETWEEN: two old partners who have not spoken in ten years. He sends: the ship is hers, and he was wrong about the engine. She answers that she'll fetch it herself. The player never goes back; the answer is the end.

prose.name: Hauling: A Message Ten Years Late
prose.briefing: An old salvager at the <Place> wants a message carried to his former partner in the same system. They haven't spoken in years.
prose.card: Private Contract. Take a message from the <Place> on <Planet> to someone in the same system. Payment on completion.

beats.objective: Talk to the old salvager at the <Place>
beats.journal: The salvager gave me a message for his old partner: the ship is hers, and he was wrong about the engine. I need to take it to her.

person.name: Emeric Shaw
hellos: You'll be the one carrying it. It isn't a long message.

_bio.from: half his life stripping wrecks with her (his lines)
_bio.why_there: grounded: his eyes won't pass for flying now (his lines)
_bio.wants: her to have the ship, and to hear he was wrong, without having to watch her face when she does (his lines)

greeting: We stripped wrecks together half our lives, then stopped speaking over an engine. There's something she should hear, and I'm the wrong one to say it.

reply: Two things. The ship's hers; my eyes have gone and I can't fly it. And I was wrong about the engine. She'll know what that means.

exchanges.prompt: What was wrong with the engine?
reply: She said it was running hot and I said she was fussing. We lost the ship we had before this one. Nobody was hurt. That was luck, not me.
Because the last time I tried, I said the wrong thing first. Say it how you like. You'll do it better than me.

beats._talk: Exchange 0 closes the talk and gives the message every player carries.

beats.objective: Give the message to his old partner at the <SecondPlace>
beats.journal: I gave his old partner the message. She's going to fetch the ship herself.

person.name: Lena Ashdown
hellos: If you're selling something, I'm not buying.

_bio.from: the same wrecks, the same years (his lines)
_bio.why_there: working alone since the split; the engine is why they split (his lines)
_bio.wants: him to say he was wrong; the ship was never the point (her lines)

greeting: Not selling? Then you're carrying something, and there's only one man who'd send me a courier instead of calling. Go on, then. What did he say?

exchanges.prompt: The ship's yours, and he was wrong about the engine.
reply: Wrong about the engine. Ten years, and he puts it second. I'll come and get the ship myself. He can have the coffee on.

exchanges.prompt: He was wrong about the engine. And the ship's yours.
reply: He said wrong, out loud? That's all I wanted. The ship can wait a day. I'm going to go and see him.

ends.journal: I told his old partner he was wrong about the engine before anything else. She's going to go and see him.

exchanges._ends: Jessica's _choice, moved verbatim into the closer field by Eliza 2026-11-09 (FrankyCLI 003d814). The pay is the beat's med: hers to change.

exchanges.prompt: He sounded like he meant it.
reply: He always does. That was never the problem.
Not once. I hear him on the general channel now and then, complaining about the weather.
